title: ASSIGNMENT – 2a
subtitle: Multi-Client Banking Message Validation Using Python Socket Programming
name: Srikrishna O S

sections.heading: AIM
paragraph: To simulate a national bank's centralized transaction validation system where multiple ATM kiosks and branch terminals communicate with a validation server simultaneously. The server validates banking transaction requests (Account Verification, Balance Enquiry, Fund Transfer Validation, Transaction Confirmation) sent by the clients and echoes each request back as an acknowledgment.

Two client-server applications are developed in Python: a TCP-based version (1a) where the server accepts multiple clients concurrently using threads, and a UDP-based version (1b) where clients send transaction requests as datagrams. The TCP and UDP implementations are then compared (1c) on connection establishment, reliability, data ordering, and communication overhead. Communication continues until a client enters "exit", after which it disconnects without affecting the other connected clients.

rows: Connection Establishment
Connection-oriented: three-way handshake before data transfer and explicit connection close
Connectionless: datagrams are sent directly with no setup or teardown
Reliability
Reliable: guarantees delivery with acknowledgments and retransmission of lost packets
Unreliable: best-effort delivery, packets may be lost without detection
Data Ordering
Ordered: segments are sequenced and delivered in the same order they were sent
Unordered: datagrams may arrive out of order
Communication Overhead
Higher: larger headers, acknowledgments, connection state and flow control
Lower: small 8-byte header and no connection state to maintain

Compare TCP and UDP
Tabulated both protocols on connection establishment, reliability, ordering, and overhead
TCP is reliable/ordered with higher overhead; UDP is faster and simpler but best-effort

sections.heading: LEARNING OUTCOMES
bullets: I implemented a TCP server that serves multiple banking clients concurrently using Python threads.
I understood that TCP requires connect()/accept() and a three-way handshake before data transfer.
I implemented a UDP server and clients using sendto()/recvfrom() without any connection setup.
I observed that the TCP server keeps serving other clients even after one client disconnects.
I compared TCP and UDP on reliability, ordering, and overhead, and saw why banks use TCP for transaction validation.
I learned that messages must be encoded to bytes before sending and decoded after receiving in both protocols.
